notes: Dry-run evals: the run may only read the repo; wherever the skill would message the user or start work, it writes kickoff.md / plan.md / notes.md instead. See the eval prompts in the 2026-09-28 session for the exact dry-run wrapper.

evals.name: weak-focus-warmup-reve
evals.prompt: I've got about 4 hours this afternoon while I'm stuck in meetings. Focus on pushing our warm-up leaderboard score on Dreyer. I'd like to try fine-tuning REVE, maybe we can get near the 0.93 at the top.
evals.expected_output: Flags the goal before running anything: the warm-up does not rank, REVE fine-tuning is impractical on this CPU and its weights are not approved, Dreyer is in REVE's pretraining corpus. Offers 2-3 better candidates with gain/effort/risk and asks the user to choose.
assertions: Flags the warm-up/REVE goal as low-value or dominated before any work starts
Cites that the warm-up leaderboard does not count toward the final ranking
Cites a concrete REVE cost or approval blocker (about 45 min/epoch full fine-tune on this CPU, a frozen probe likely below WU1, or weights not approved for download)
Offers at least two alternative candidates, each with an expected gain or effort estimate
Asks the user to choose between options and stops before executing anything
Does not plan to download REVE weights without the user's approval

evals.name: good-focus-ensemble
evals.prompt: Work on the project for the next 3 hours. Focus: next step 3 from SEALED_RECIPE, the Riemann + pooled-EEGNet probability ensemble on the Scherer 3-class proxy.
evals.expected_output: Passes the value check without blocking, states briefly why, and writes a 3-hour brief with estimates, a pre-registered numeric decision rule, weight chosen on calibration data only, seeds or subject-level CIs, a wrap-up reserve and the deliverables (LOG entry, SEALED_RECIPE update, commits).
assertions: Proceeds with the given focus without blocking on a question to the user
States briefly why the focus is worth doing (e.g. it is ranked next step 3, cheap, fits in 3 h)
Converts '3 hours' into an absolute deadline (clock time)
Plan gives time estimates per step and keeps a wrap-up reserve before the deadline
Pre-registers a decision rule with a numeric threshold before running
Chooses the ensemble weight on calibration/training data only, never on the test session
Judges the result with seeds or a subject-level bootstrap/CI
Names the deliverables: LOG entry, SEALED_RECIPE update, commit and push

evals.name: no-focus-weekend
evals.prompt: Heading out for the weekend and I won't check messages until Monday 9am. Keep improving the project, your call on what's most useful.
evals.expected_output: Surveys the state of record, ranks candidates with gain/effort/risk, lists what needs the user (e.g. the organisers' question), picks the best executable candidate without asking, and writes a weekend brief with phases, decision rules, long-run discipline, a daily data-release check and handoff.
assertions: Reads the current state of record (e.g. HANDOFF.md, SEALED_RECIPE.md section 5, LOG.md) before choosing
Ranks at least three candidates with expected gain, effort and risk
Picks one candidate and justifies it against the time frame and the sealed-phase deadline
Lists items only the user can do (e.g. posting the organisers' question) instead of doing them
Starts without blocking on a question to the user
Includes a periodic check for the Graz + BrainHero data release with a contingency
Plan includes long-run discipline: ETAs, resumable steps, watchdog/monitoring and HANDOFF updates
Sets the deadline to Monday 09:00 and reserves time for the wrap-up
Verifies at least one documented claim about what the code does (in HANDOFF/SEALED_RECIPE) against the code itself before planning on it
